headline: Betel leaves and zarda found in suspicious bags at metro stations
summary: Mirpur-10 and Farmgate stations were briefly shut or secured after abandoned bags triggered bomb scares, but police confirmed no explosives were found.
details: Suspicious bags found at Mirpur-10 and Farmgate metro stations today triggered a security scare, leading to the temporary closure of the Mirpur-10 station.
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) confirmed that neither item contained explosives or hazardous materials.
At Mirpur-10, the CTTC bomb disposal unit used a frangible disruptor to neutralize a container-like object detected by an X-ray scan, only to find betel leaves and zarda (chewing tobacco).
A separate abandoned sack found near Farmgate station was manually examined by bomb disposal personnel and found to be safe.
Mirpur-10 station was reopened at approximately 1:40 PM after the security clearance.
The DMP has urged the public not to panic over unverified reports during such security operations.
caption:
Betel leaves and zarda! That's all that was inside the 'bombs' that caused panic at two Dhaka metro stations today.

Suspicious bags found at Mirpur-10 and Farmgate metro stations today triggered a security scare, leading to the temporary closure of the Mirpur-10 station.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) confirmed that neither item contained explosives or hazardous materials.

At Mirpur-10, the CTTC bomb disposal unit used a frangible disruptor to neutralize a container-like object detected by an X-ray scan, only to find betel leaves and zarda (chewing tobacco).

A separate abandoned sack found near Farmgate station was manually examined by bomb disposal personnel and found to be safe.

Mirpur-10 station was reopened at approximately 1:40 PM after the security clearance.

The DMP has urged the public not to panic over unverified reports during such security operations.

headline_marked: US makes [[$20,000 visa bond permanent]] for Bangladeshis
headline: US makes $20,000 visa bond permanent for Bangladeshis
summary: The Trump administration is making a visa bond program permanent for citizens of 50 countries, including Bangladesh, to prevent illegal overstays.
details: The US State Department is making a visa bond program permanent, requiring applicants from 50 countries, including Bangladesh, to potentially deposit up to $20,000 to obtain a visa.
The rule applies to 'B1' and 'B2' visas, which are typically used for business and tourism. Consular officers will determine the specific bond amount for individual applicants.
The Trump administration stated that data from a 2025 pilot project showed the bond was effective in ensuring visa holders complied with their terms and returned home.
The new rule will take effect on August 3, following its publication in the Federal Register. Out of the 50 affected countries, 30 are located in Africa.
US officials claim the policy aims to stop tourists from staying illegally after their visas expire. However, immigration experts argue this will discourage legitimate travel to the United States.
Human rights activists have criticized the move as part of an aggressive immigration crackdown that may fuel racial discrimination and undermine the right to fair trial and free speech.
caption:
A US visa could now cost you an extra $20,000. The Trump administration is making this bond permanent for Bangladeshis and 49 other nations.

The US State Department is making a visa bond program permanent, requiring applicants from 50 countries, including Bangladesh, to potentially deposit up to $20,000 to obtain a visa.

The rule applies to 'B1' and 'B2' visas, which are typically used for business and tourism. Consular officers will determine the specific bond amount for individual applicants.

The Trump administration stated that data from a 2025 pilot project showed the bond was effective in ensuring visa holders complied with their terms and returned home.

The new rule will take effect on August 3, following its publication in the Federal Register. Out of the 50 affected countries, 30 are located in Africa.

US officials claim the policy aims to stop tourists from staying illegally after their visas expire. However, immigration experts argue this will discourage legitimate travel to the United States.

Human rights activists have criticized the move as part of an aggressive immigration crackdown that may fuel racial discrimination and undermine the right to fair trial and free speech.
